newsitem.title: USA: U.S. judge narrows questioning of DNC aide Huang.
newsitem.headline: U.S. judge narrows questioning of DNC aide Huang.

text.p: A federal judge made clear Tuesday that Democratic Party fundraiser John Huang may be questioned only about the search for documents involving Commerce Department trade missions.
"Mr. Huang's life is not on trial," U.S. District Judge Royce Lamberth said of the former Commerce Department official. "I did not say all questions can be asked."

His comments came at a court hearing just minutes before the scheduled start of Huang's questioning by the conservative legal group Judicial Watch in a freedom-of-information case against the Commerce Department.
Huang has come under fire over the legality of campaign contributions he solicited as a Democratic National Committee fundraiser. But those activities are not at issue in the civil lawsuit.

Lamberth emphasised that questioning should cover only the search for documents under the freedom-of-information laws concerning trade missions led by the late Commerce Secretary Ron Brown. Judicial Watch's 2-year-old lawsuit claims the Commerce Department used the trade missions improperly to raise funds for Democrats and failed to release requested documents about the missions.
Huang's attorneys filed a last-minute objection to the group's demands that he turn over various documents, claiming it was unduly burdensome and citing time constraints and other grounds.
The group wants to question another former Commerce Department official, Melinda Lee. But Larry Klayman, the group's general counsel, said her lawyers told him she would not be available this week.

Judicial Watch also issued a subpoena for any Commerce Department documents held in a public storage facility owned by Brown's wife, Alma. Her attorney, Reid Weingarten, said the facility only had documents involving a brief period before Brown's confirmation. "The long and short of it is there were no documents in the storage facility (related) to this litigation," he said.
